nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a substitution score and $g$ a gap score. For all sequences $x$ and $y$ there is an infix $l$ of $y$ such that the Needleman–Wunsch score of $x$ against $l$ (with $\sigma$ and $g$) equals the fitting score of $x$ against $y$.
nodes.title: The fitting score is attained

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a substitution score and $g$ a gap score. For all sequences $x$ and $y$ there is an overlap pair $(x', y')$ of $x$ and $y$ such that the Needleman–Wunsch score of $x'$ against $y'$ (with $\sigma$ and $g$) equals the overlap score of $x$ and $y$.
nodes.title: The overlap score is attained

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a substitution score and $g$ a gap score. For all sequences $x$ and $y$, the fitting score of $x$ against $y$ is at most the local score of $x$ and $y$, both taken with $\sigma$ and $g$.
nodes.title: The fitting score is at most the local score

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a substitution score, $g$ a gap score, $x$ and $y$ sequences and $b$ an integer. If the Needleman–Wunsch score of $x$ against every infix of $y$ (with $\sigma$ and $g$) is at most $b$, then the fitting score of $x$ against $y$ is at most $b$.
nodes.title: Upper bounds on the fitting score

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a substitution score and $g$ a gap score. The fitting score of a sequence $x$ against a sequence $y$ is the maximum, over all infixes $l$ of $y$ (including the empty one), of the Needleman–Wunsch score of $x$ against $l$ with $\sigma$ and $g$: the best global alignment score of $x$ against a substring of $y$.
nodes.title: Fitting score

nodes.summary: The infixes of a sequence $y$ are its contiguous substrings: the sequences $l$ such that $y$ is the concatenation of $s$, $l$ and $t$ for some sequences $s$ and $t$, including the empty sequence and $y$ itself. They are listed as the suffixes of the prefixes of $y$, so the list can contain repetitions.
nodes.title: Infixes

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a substitution score and $g$ a gap score. If $l$ is an infix of a sequence $y$, then for every sequence $x$ the Needleman–Wunsch score of $x$ against $l$ is at most the fitting score of $x$ against $y$, both taken with $\sigma$ and $g$.
nodes.title: Infix scores are at most the fitting score

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a substitution score and $g$ a gap score. If $(x', y')$ is an overlap pair of sequences $x$ and $y$, then the Needleman–Wunsch score of $x'$ against $y'$ is at most the overlap score of $x$ and $y$, both taken with $\sigma$ and $g$.
nodes.title: Overlap-pair scores are at most the overlap score

nodes.summary: The overlap pairs of sequences $x$ and $y$ are the pairs $(x', y')$ in which $x'$ is a suffix of $x$ and $y'$ is a prefix of $y$, or $x'$ is a prefix of $x$ and $y'$ is a suffix of $y$. Prefixes and suffixes include the empty sequence and the whole sequence; the pairs are listed with the suffix–prefix pairs first, and the list can contain repetitions.
nodes.title: Overlap pairs

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a substitution score and $g$ a gap score. For all sequences $x$ and $y$, the overlap score of $x$ and $y$ is at most the local score of $x$ and $y$, both taken with $\sigma$ and $g$.
nodes.title: The overlap score is at most the local score

nodes.summary: Fix a substitution score $\sigma$ and a gap score $g$, and sequences $s$ and $t$. If an integer $b$ is at least the Needleman–Wunsch score of every overlap pair of $s$ and $t$ (a suffix of $s$ with a prefix of $t$, or a prefix of $s$ with a suffix of $t$), then the overlap score of $s$ and $t$ is at most $b$.
nodes.title: Upper bounds for the overlap score

nodes.summary: For every substitution score $\sigma$, gap score $g$ and sequences $s$ and $t$, the overlap score of $s$ and $t$ is at least $0$.
nodes.title: The overlap score is nonnegative

nodes.summary: Given a substitution score $\sigma$ and a gap score $g$, the overlap score of sequences $s$ and $t$ is the maximum, with floor $0$, of the Needleman–Wunsch scores of the overlap pairs of $s$ and $t$: the pairs $(s', t')$ where $s'$ is a suffix of $s$ and $t'$ a prefix of $t$, or $s'$ is a prefix of $s$ and $t'$ a suffix of $t$.
nodes.title: Overlap alignment score

nodes.summary: For every list $L$ of integers, the maximum of $L$ with floor $0$ (which is $0$ for the empty list) is at least $0$.
nodes.title: The floored list maximum is nonnegative

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
